frozen_original.title: Trump Ends CIA Covert Programs in Multiple Countries
frozen_original.synopsis: In 2025, the Trump administration ordered the termination of numerous CIA covert action programs operating in multiple countries, reportedly including counter-proliferation operations targeting adversary weapons programs, human intelligence networks in rival states, and influence operations countering Russian and Chinese disinformation. Former CIA directors warned that shutting down long-established programs dismantled years of relationship-building with foreign assets and partner services that could not be quickly reconstituted. The terminations were described by officials as driven by a combination of cost-cutting ideology, skepticism of the intelligence community, and deference to foreign governments that had complained about US operations. The hollowing out of covert capabilities was seen as a strategic windfall for Moscow and Beijing.

proposal.original_claim_summary: Trump Organization Loans to Trump at Favorable Rates — Tax Manipulation Scheme
proposal.original_synopsis: Prior to his presidency, Trump engaged in complex financial transactions with the Trump Organization in which loans to himself at artificially favorable interest rates were used to shift income and minimize tax liability. The New York Attorney General's investigation and subsequent civil fraud lawsuit revealed a pattern of asset valuation manipulation for tax and lending purposes. Trump properties were valued higher when seeking loans from banks and lower when calculating taxes. A New York court found Trump liable for fraud, ordered him to pay $364 million in penalties, and barred him from serving as an officer of New York corporations.

frozen_original.title: Immigration enforcement uses facial recognition on social media profiles
frozen_original.synopsis: ICE and DHS deployed facial recognition technology to scan social media profiles, using it as a tool to identify and target undocumented immigrants and political dissenters. The program applied facial recognition algorithms across multiple social media platforms to match profile photos against government biometric databases, enabling mass identification of individuals without their knowledge or consent. Privacy advocates warned the program created a surveillance dragnet disproportionately targeting immigrant and minority communities.
